div.ab: Concerning the law of the Mercians (Mircna laga)

ab.hi: On the Law of the Mercians

div.note: Liebermann prints D (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 201, p. 102, after Norðleod, c. 1060; by its author or someone using or influenced by him), O (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 190, p. 418, another hand c. 1075, after the Confessional and Penitential of Egbert) and H (Textus Roffensis f. 39v, after Að, c. 1120, without heading, on a new line), with Ld, the Quadripartitus and the Instituta Cnuti III 42–43.4. K is H, which has no heading, so K is empty here; D is also given here. D's heading is in red; the Quadripartitus heading is not original. Liebermann dates Mirce c. 920–c. 970. Clause number standardised from ‘Mirce Inscr.’.; AT: added from Whitelock p. 477, October 2026 (Whitelock’s footnotes); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “1002–23 (Whitelock); 1006–8 (Rabin)”, now “c.920–c.970 (Liebermann); 1002–23 (Whitelock); 1006–8 (Rabin)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.920–c.970 (Liebermann); 1002–23 (Whitelock); 1006–8 (Rabin)”, now “c.920–c.970 (Liebermann, I p. 462); 1002–23 (Whitelock, EHD p. 475); 1006–8 (Rabin)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “D 462; O 462; Q 463; German 462”; 7 rows of Mirce); AX: pages in Rabin (text / translation), checked against Rabin (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “14”, now “14 / 15”; 2 rows of Mirce)

note.seg: Die Überschrift in DO erregt zwar inhaltlich kein Bedenken gegen die Authentizität. Belegt aber ist sie durch die andere Hss.-Klasse hlq nicht; denn was Q's jüngste Rezension überschreibt, mochte sie, wie sonst, nur dem Lateintexte entnehmen

The heading in DO does not, as far as its content goes, raise any doubt as to its authenticity. But it is not attested by the other class of MSS, hlq; for what Q’s youngest recension provides with a heading it may, as elsewhere, have taken merely from the Latin text
Dativ laga auch 2. 3, ferner I Cn 6, 2a; 3; vgl. Wb S. 48 Sp. 3. 129 Sp. 3
Dative laga also 2. 3, and further I Cn 6, 2a; 3; cf. Wb p. 48 col. 3. 129 col. 3

The texts I include under this heading are those called by Liebermann Geþyncðo, Norðleoda laga, Mircna laga. Að and Hadbot, and printed by him, I, 456–69. Thorpe has the three first, in a different order, I, 186–93. The five texts occur in C.C.C.C., MS. 201, a manuscript with connections with Archbishop Wulfstan, and D.Bethurum has produced good reasons for assigning the collection to this prelate, who was deeply interested in this matter. The last three are also in C.C.C.C.. MS. 190, another manuscript connected with Wulfstan. All five, but not as a group or in order, are in the Textus Roffensis, and the authors of Quadripartitus and the Instituta Cnuti use them. Much of what is known of status in Anglo-Saxon times comes from these texts, which should not be regarded as official enactments but as a private compilation. [Her footnote 2: No. 52 in the 1955 edition] [Her footnote 3: Journ. Engl. and Germ. Phil., xlix, 449–63]
